title: Turning Effect of Forces
seo_title: Secondary 3 Physics: Turning Effect of Forces Worksheets (O-Level 6091 with Answers)
standard_code: O-Level Physics (6091): Turning Effect of Forces
standard_text: Describe the moment of a force in terms of its turning effect and relate this to everyday examples; recall and apply moment = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot; state the principle of moments for a body in equilibrium and apply it to new situations; show understanding that the weight of a body may be taken as acting at its centre of gravity; describe qualitatively the effect of the position of the centre of gravity on the stability of objects (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Physics 6091 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 O-Level Physics worksheets on the turning effect of forces: moments, the principle of moments, balanced beams and see-saws, centre of gravity and stability. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: In equilibrium: clockwise moments = anticlockwise moments.
body_html:
How to think about it

A moment is the turning effect of a force.

  • Moment = F × d, where d is the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of the force (N m). Change cm into m first.
  • Principle of moments: in equilibrium, total clockwise moment = total anticlockwise moment about any point, and the resultant force is zero.
  • A uniform object's weight acts at its centre (its centre of gravity). A low centre of gravity and a wide base make an object stable.
Example

40 N at 0.3 m from a pivot balances F at 0.6 m. F?

F × 0.6 = 40 × 0.3 = 12

Answer: 20 N

Example

A 15 N force acts 20 cm from a nut. Moment?

20 cm = 0.20 m

15 × 0.20

Answer: 3 N m

Common mistakes

  • Dividing force by distance. Moment = force × distance.
  • Forgetting to change cm into m when the answer is in N m.
  • Using the slanting distance instead of the perpendicular distance.
  • Forgetting the weight of a uniform beam, which acts at its centre.

faq.q: How do you use the principle of moments?
faq.a: Take moments about the pivot. Add all the clockwise moments and all the anticlockwise moments, set them equal and solve for the unknown.
A low centre of gravity and a wide base, so the line of action of the weight stays inside the base when it is tilted.

faq.q: Where does the weight of a uniform beam act?
faq.a: At its centre. Include it as a force at the middle of the beam when you take moments.

items.q: A force of 60 N gives a moment of 30 N m about a pivot. How far from the pivot does it act?
items.e: d = moment ÷ F = 30 ÷ 60 = 0.5 m.

items.q: Why is a long spanner easier to use than a short one?
c: The same force gives a larger moment because the distance is larger.
items.e: A longer lever arm gives more turning effect.

items.q: A force of 8 N acts at right angles to a crowbar at a distance of 50 cm from the pivot. What is the moment in N m?
items.e: Change cm to m first: 50 cm = 0.5 m. Moment = 8 × 0.5 = 4 N m.

items.q: A force of 8 N acts at right angles to a spanner at a distance of 40 cm from the pivot. What is the moment in N m?
items.e: Change cm to m first: 40 cm = 0.4 m. Moment = 8 × 0.4 = 3.2 N m.

items.q: A force of 40 N acts at right angles on a tap handle, 0.1 m from the pivot. What is the moment of the force?
items.e: Moment = F × d = 40 × 0.1 = 4 N m.

items.q: A moment of 3 N m is needed to turn a tap handle. The force is applied 0.6 m from the pivot. What force is needed?
items.e: F = moment ÷ d = 3 ÷ 0.6 = 5 N.

items.q: A force of 30 N is applied to a crowbar 0.2 m from the pivot. What is the moment?
items.e: moment = force × distance from pivot = 30 × 0.2.

items.q: A moment of 25 N m is needed to turn a wheelbarrow handle. The force is applied 0.5 m from the pivot. What force is needed?
items.e: F = moment ÷ d = 25 ÷ 0.5 = 50 N.

items.q: A moment of 3 N m is needed to turn a wheelbarrow handle. The force is applied 0.6 m from the pivot. What force is needed?
items.e: F = moment ÷ d = 3 ÷ 0.6 = 5 N.

items.q: Which change makes an object more stable?
c: lowering its centre of gravity and widening its base
items.e: The weight's line of action stays inside the base for a larger tilt.

items.q: State the principle of moments.
c: The forces on each side are always equal.
Moments only act on moving objects.
The heavier side always goes down.
For a body in equilibrium, the sum of clockwise moments about any point equals the sum of anticlockwise moments about that point.
items.e: Also, the resultant force must be zero.

items.q: A force of 80 N acts at right angles to a door handle at a distance of 80 cm from the pivot. What is the moment in N m?
items.e: Change cm to m first: 80 cm = 0.8 m. Moment = 80 × 0.8 = 64 N m.

items.q: How can you find the centre of gravity of a flat irregular card?
c: Measure its longest side and halve it.
Hang it freely from two points and draw a plumb line from each; the lines cross at the centre of gravity.
Balance it on a spring balance.
items.e: The plumb-line method.

c: It must be at the same height.
The resultant force is zero and the resultant moment is zero.

the point where the whole weight of the object appears to act

items.q: A wheelbarrow carries a 400 N load 0.5 m from the wheel. The handles are 1.6 m from the wheel. What upward force at the handles lifts it? (ignore the barrow's weight)
Which statement best describes the stability of a bus with many passengers standing on the upper deck?
c: less stable: high centre of gravity and narrow base
unstable: any small tilt makes it fall
less stable: the centre of gravity is raised
more stable: the heavy base lowers the centre of gravity
items.e: A bus with many passengers standing on the upper deck: less stable: the centre of gravity is raised.

items.q: A uniform beam 2 m long weighs 150 N. It is pivoted 0.6 m from one end. What weight must hang from that end to keep it horizontal?
items.e: The beam's weight acts at its centre, 0.4 m from the pivot. W × 0.6 = 150 × 0.4, so W = 100 N.

items.q: When does a tilted object topple over?
c: as soon as it is tilted
when the line of action of its weight falls outside its base
items.e: The weight then gives a moment that turns it further.

items.q: A pair of scissors cuts card more easily near the pivot. Why?
c: For the same force at the handles, the force on the card is larger near the pivot.
items.e: Moment at the handle = moment at the card.

items.q: A uniform plank 6 m long is pivoted 0.6 m from one end. It balances horizontally when an 800 N weight hangs from that end. What is the weight of the plank?
items.e: Its weight W acts at the centre, 2.4 m from the pivot. W × 2.4 = 800 × 0.6, so W = 200 N.

items.q: Which statement best describes the stability of a cone standing on its base?
c: less stable: high centre of gravity and narrow base
stable: low centre of gravity and wide base
more stable: the heavy base lowers the centre of gravity
unstable: any small tilt makes it fall
items.e: A cone standing on its base: stable: low centre of gravity and wide base.

items.q: Why do double-decker buses carry heavy items low down?
c: to increase the moment of the driver
to keep the centre of gravity low so the bus is stable when it leans
items.e: A low centre of gravity resists toppling.

items.q: A uniform 2.0 m plank weighs 80 N and rests on a pivot at its centre. What weight at one end keeps it balanced?
items.e: Its weight acts through the pivot, so it gives no moment.

items.e: The plank's weight acts at its centre, 1.2 m from the pivot. W × 0.8 = 50 × 1.2, so W = 75 N.

items.q: A tall bookshelf is fixed to the wall with a bracket. Why?
c: It has a high centre of gravity and could topple if pulled.
items.e: The bracket stops it turning.

items.q: Which statement best describes the stability of a racing car with a low, wide body?

items.e: A racing car with a low, wide body: very stable: low centre of gravity and wide base.

items.q: Which statement best describes the stability of a tall, narrow vase?

less stable: the centre of gravity is raised

items.q: Which statement best describes the stability of a cone balanced on its tip?

more stable: the heavy base lowers the centre of gravity
unstable: any small tilt makes it fall

items.q: A uniform plank 5 m long is pivoted 0.5 m from one end. It balances horizontally when a 120 N weight hangs from that end. What is the weight of the plank?
items.e: Its weight W acts at the centre, 2 m from the pivot. W × 2 = 120 × 0.5, so W = 30 N.

items.q: A uniform beam 1 m long is pivoted 0.4 m from one end. It balances horizontally when a 30 N weight hangs from that end. What is the weight of the beam?

items.q: Which statement best describes the stability of a table lamp with a heavy base?

items.e: A table lamp with a heavy base: more stable: the heavy base lowers the centre of gravity.

items.q: A 30 N force pushes a door 0.8 m from the hinges at an angle, not at right angles. Why is the moment less than 24 N m?
c: Moments do not depend on angle.
The perpendicular distance from the hinge to the line of the force is less than 0.8 m.
items.e: Only the perpendicular distance counts.
